prompt.context_jp: 甘春総合病院の検査室___、静かな緊張に満ちていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 甘春総合病院の検査室___、静かな緊張に満ちていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the examination room as the topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: は establishes the examination room as the topic/setting the narrator will describe. It frames the scene for the reader.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce it as new information in a reporting sense, which is less natural for scene-setting narration. を doesn't fit — the room isn't an object here.

prompt.context_jp: 通常のマンモグラフィーでは決して映らないような、細くしなやかな影___確かにそこにあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 細くしなやかな影___確かにそこにあった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the newly discovered shadow.

feedback.correct_en: が marks the shadow as newly presented information — this is the moment of discovery. 'There was indeed...' is classic existential/new-info が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would suggest the shadow is already a known topic, which contradicts the discovery context. に doesn't fit syntactically.

prompt.context_jp: モニターの光___、その表情に静かな影を落としていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: モニターの光___、その表情に静かな影を落としていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'the light from the monitor' as the subject of this descriptive action.

feedback.correct_en: が presents the monitor light as a new observational detail in the scene — the narrator zooms in on this subject performing an action.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a topic-contrast, which doesn't fit this descriptive narration. で (means) doesn't fit the verb 落とす here with light as agent.

contrast_examples.en: Light (as topic) doesn't cast a shadow (contrast).

prompt.context_jp: 検査室の空気___、細い糸を張ったように張り詰めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 検査室の空気___、細い糸を張ったように張り詰めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'the air in the room' as the topic being characterized.

feedback.correct_en: は marks the air as the topic the narrator characterizes with a state. This is a general description, not a reporting of new occurrence.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal new-information discovery, unnatural for stative description. を is grammatically wrong.

contrast_examples.jp: 空気は張り詰めていた。

prompt.context_jp: その動きを見て取った小野寺の声___、鋭く飛ぶ。
prompt.prompt_jp: その動きを見て取った小野寺の声___、鋭く飛ぶ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Onodera's voice entering the scene.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces the voice as a new, suddenly appearing element in the scene — the sharp interjection.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it an already-known topic, losing the sudden-event feel. に doesn't fit as the subject marker.

contrast_examples.en: His voice was low (describing a known voice).

prompt.context_jp: 広瀬___指先を震わせながら、装置のスイッチに手を伸ばした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 広瀬___指先を震わせながら、装置のスイッチに手を伸ばした。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Hirose as the topic of this action sequence.

feedback.correct_en: は marks Hirose as the established topic whose action we're following. The focus is on what he does, not on identifying who it is.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark exhaustive identification ('it is Hirose who...'), unnatural in continued narration. を is ungrammatical here.

prompt.context_jp: 同じ日の午後、診察室では今日子___椅子に浅く腰かけていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 診察室では今日子___椅子に浅く腰かけていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Kyoko being introduced into this new scene.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces Kyoko into the new scene (the exam room). The topic position is already taken by 診察室では, so が naturally marks the subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は can't co-occur comfortably as a second topic in this では構文. を is ungrammatical.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋では男が座っていた。
contrast_examples.en: In the room, a man was sitting.

contrast_examples.jp: 男は部屋で座っていた。
contrast_examples.en: The man was sitting in the room.

prompt.context_jp: 医師___職務に忠実であろうと、努めて中庸な口調を保っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 医師___職務に忠実であろうと、努めて中庸な口調を保っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'the doctor' as the topic of the sentence.

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes 'the doctor' — the sentence then explains his approach and reasoning. This is a characterization, not a report of new occurrence.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal new-info identification, unnatural when the doctor has already been introduced. に is ungrammatical here.

prompt.context_jp: 今日子の表情に、驚きも嘆きも浮かばぬの___、かえって杏の胸を締めつけた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 驚きも嘆きも浮かばぬの___、かえって杏の胸を締めつけた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the nominalized clause as subject.

feedback.correct_en: が marks the nominalized subject (the fact that no reaction appeared). Nominalized のだ-type subjects in such emotive reporting take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize it awkwardly in a cause-effect description. を doesn't fit — this clause is the subject of 締めつけた.

contrast_examples.jp: 返事がないのが気になる。
contrast_examples.en: The lack of reply bothers me.
There's no reply but it's fine.

prompt.context_jp: がん自体は大きいですけど 幸い転移___していませんから
prompt.prompt_jp: がん自体は大きいですけど 幸い転移___していません
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle expressing contrastive emphasis on 'metastasis' not having occurred.

feedback.correct_en: は carries contrastive focus: the cancer is big, BUT metastasis specifically has not happened. は highlights this positive counterpoint.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just state existence/subject neutrally, losing the contrastive 'at least this hasn't happened' nuance. を doesn't fit with しない in this pattern.

prompt.context_jp: 杏の胸に、ふっと熱いもの___込み上げた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 杏の胸に、ふっと熱いもの___込み上げた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'something hot' welling up.

feedback.correct_en: が marks the emergent emotion as new, spontaneously arising — classic が for sudden inner occurrences (涙が出る, 熱いものが込み上げる).
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize an already-known thing, unnatural for a spontaneous welling-up. を doesn't fit with intransitive 込み上げる.

prompt.context_jp: 今日子の頬に、堪えていた涙___ひと筋こぼれ落ちた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 堪えていた涙___ひと筋こぼれ落ちた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the tear newly appearing.

feedback.correct_en: が presents the tear as a newly observed event — the moment it falls. Spontaneous physical reactions take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark the tears as pre-established topic, breaking the discovery-moment feel. も would mean 'also/even', not fitting.

prompt.context_jp: 病院の玄関___出た今日子を、恋人の公太が心配そうに待っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 病院の玄関___出た今日子
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the point of departure through which Kyoko exits.

feedback.correct_en: を with movement verbs like 出る marks the place one exits from (departure point passed through).
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a destination, opposite meaning. で would mark the location of an action, not the exit point.

prompt.context_jp: 今日子を、恋人の公太___心配そうに待っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 恋人の公太___心配そうに待っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Kota, newly introduced into the scene.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces Kota as new information — this is his first appearance in the chapter, introduced via descriptive apposition '恋人の公太'.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose Kota as a known topic, which he isn't yet. を is the object marker already used for Kyoko.

contrast_examples.en: My boyfriend is kind (characterizing known topic).

prompt.context_jp: 私 胸 なくなっちゃうんだよ？
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___胸 なくなっちゃうんだよ？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle to mark 'I' as the topic of this emotional outburst.

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes 'I' — 'As for me, I'm going to lose my breast.' The focus is on Kyoko's own situation being described.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it exhaustive identification ('I'm the one who...'), odd here. を doesn't work for 'I' as the experiencer.

contrast_examples.en: I'm the one who'll be in trouble (exhaustive).

prompt.context_jp: それを制するように立ちはだかったの___、意外な人物だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 立ちはだかったの___、意外な人物だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the cleft construction 'the one who stood in the way was...'

feedback.correct_en: は functions in the cleft construction 'Xのは、Yだった' — 'the one who X was Y'. This frames the known action and reveals the unexpected agent.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the nominalized clause the new-info subject, but here the structure needs は to set up the reveal. を is ungrammatical.

contrast_examples.en: The one who came was him.

prompt.context_jp: 呼び声に振り向いた杏の顔___、瞬時に強張った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 杏の顔___、瞬時に強張った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking An's face as the subject of a sudden change.

feedback.correct_en: が marks the face as the subject of a sudden involuntary change — a reported event, not a topicalization.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would characterize the face generally, but here we have a specific moment of reaction. を is ungrammatical with intransitive 強張る.

contrast_examples.en: His face was pale (describing a state).

prompt.context_jp: 「___です つまり 良性の腫瘤です！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___です つまり 良性の腫瘤です！」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word Hirose uses to describe the tumor's physical consistency on elastography.

feedback.correct_en: やわらかい (soft) is the elastography finding — soft tumors are benign, hard ones are malignant.
feedback.incorrect_en: あかるい (bright) describes light, not tissue. ちいさい (small) refers to size, which doesn't determine benign/malignant on elastography.

contrast_examples.jp: やわらかい腫瘤は良性。
硬い腫瘤は悪性の可能性。
contrast_examples.en: A hard tumor may be malignant.

prompt.context_jp: 「___ 甘春先生にも 診てもらってくださいね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___ 甘春先生にも 診てもらってくださいね」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the set phrase meaning 'just in case / to be safe.'

feedback.correct_en: 念のため = 'just to be safe/just in case' — the standard phrase when recommending extra verification.
feedback.incorrect_en: ついでに ('while you're at it') sounds too casual for a medical recommendation. もちろん ('of course') doesn't fit the hedge of making an additional check.

contrast_examples.en: Buy it while you're at it.

prompt.context_jp: 右胸を___すれば 命に別条はないでしょう
prompt.prompt_jp: 右胸を___すれば 命に別条はないでしょう
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the medical term meaning 'complete surgical removal.'

feedback.correct_en: 全摘 (ぜんてき) means complete surgical excision — the standard medical term for full mastectomy.
feedback.incorrect_en: 全開 means 'fully open' (unrelated). 全快 means 'full recovery' — different concept.

prompt.context_jp: 「当たり前でしょ 女に___はない」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「当たり前でしょ 女に___はない」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that completes the idiom 'a woman doesn't take back her word.'

feedback.correct_en: 二言(にごん)はない = 'won't say two different things / won't go back on one's word.' Classic idiom.
feedback.incorrect_en: 二度 (twice) and 二心 (treachery) don't form this fixed idiom. The phrase specifically uses 二言.

contrast_examples.en: A man doesn't go back on his word.

prompt.context_jp: 「えっ？ ___ですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「えっ？ ___ですか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word meaning 'bragging about one's romantic partner.'

feedback.correct_en: のろけ specifically means lovingly bragging about one's partner — exactly what Hayama's '大切な人のためにも' comment prompted.
feedback.incorrect_en: つぶやき is just 'a murmur'; ひとりごと is 'talking to oneself' — neither captures the partner-bragging nuance.

prompt.context_jp: その言葉を口にする瞬間には、幾度経験しても慣れることのない___が伴った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 幾度経験しても慣れることのない___が伴った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun that captures the emotional 'weight' of delivering a cancer diagnosis.

feedback.correct_en: 重み (weight) is the standard metaphor for emotional heaviness/gravity of words — matches the chapter title '告知の重み'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 厚み (thickness) and 深み (depth) are physical/metaphorical but don't collocate with words-you-must-say gravity.

prompt.context_jp: エラストモードに切り替えれば、腫瘤の硬さから良性と悪性の___が可能になる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 腫瘤の硬さから良性と悪性の___が可能になる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun meaning 'differentiation/discrimination between two things.'

feedback.correct_en: 判別 specifically means distinguishing between categories (benign vs. malignant). This is the clinical term.
feedback.incorrect_en: 判断 is general 'judgment', 判定 is 'verdict/determination' — both broader. 判別 best captures A-vs-B discrimination.

prompt.context_jp: 「私 生きるために 決断したあなたを 心から ___しています」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「決断したあなたを 心から ___しています」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'to respect/admire deeply.'

feedback.correct_en: 尊敬 = respect/admire a person. An admires Kyoko's decision as a person.
feedback.incorrect_en: 尊重 means respecting rights/opinions abstractly, less personal. 信頼 means trust, a different emotional register.

prompt.context_jp: 「こっ これは… ___状の非浸潤性乳がんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___状の非浸潤性乳がんです」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word Igarashi uses to describe the shape of the carcinoma pattern.

feedback.correct_en: クモの巣状 ('web/spider-web-shaped') describes the branching, delicate pattern of this type of ductal carcinoma.
feedback.incorrect_en: ひし形 (diamond-shape) and 扇 (fan-shape) don't fit the branching, filament-like image described in the story.

prompt.context_jp: 公太がパートナーとの外見の変化を軽く受け止めている場面
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for 'changes in appearance happen to both of us'?

choices.text: 見た目が変わるのなんて お互いさまだよ
見た目を変わるの お互いさまだよ
見た目が変わるのが お互いさまよ

feedback.correct_en: お互いさま is a set phrase for 'it goes both ways / same for both of us.' The nominalizer のなんて adds the dismissive 'something like' feel appropriate for Kota's reassurance.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) uses を incorrectly with intransitive 変わる. (c) adds an extra が that breaks the natural rhythm of the お互いさま phrasing.

contrast_examples.jp: 困るのはお互いさまだ。

prompt.context_jp: 今日子が杏に対して対等なライバル宣言をする場面
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for 'I won't lose to you' with Kyoko's gentle-but-firm tone?

choices.text: あなたには 負けませんから
あなたに 負けないですから
あなたを 負けませんから

feedback.correct_en: 負ける takes に for the opponent, and には adds contrastive emphasis ('to YOU, I won't lose'). The 〜ませんから ending gives a determined, polite close.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) drops the contrastive には, weakening the challenge. (c) uses を incorrectly — 負ける is intransitive and takes に.

prompt.context_jp: 杏が乳がんの発症率を説明する場面
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is most natural for '1 in 11 people get breast cancer'?

choices.text: 乳がんは 11人に1人がなる病気です
乳がんは 11人の1人がなる病気です
乳がんは 11人で1人がなる病気です

feedback.correct_en: 〜人に1人 is the fixed Japanese pattern for 'X in N people' statistics.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜人の1人 (b) sounds like 'one of 11 specific people'. 〜人で1人 (c) sounds like 'with 11 people, one becomes...' — not standard.

prompt.context_jp: 杏が今日子に手術を説明する場面
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for 'there is a risk of recurrence from there'?

choices.text: そこから 再発する恐れがあります
そこから 再発する心配があります
そこから 再発する怖さがあります

feedback.correct_en: 〜恐れがある is the standard formal medical/professional phrasing for 'there is a risk of ~'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心配がある is more personal ('I'm worried'). 怖さがある ('there is a scariness') is not natural in professional medical speech.

contrast_examples.en: There is a risk of earthquake.

prompt.context_jp: 小野寺が広瀬に対して不機嫌に答える場面
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for Onodera's gruff 'I already knew that'?

choices.text: そんなこと 言われなくても分かってる
そんなこと 言わなくても分かってる
そんなこと 言わないでも分かってる

feedback.correct_en: 言われなくても (passive 'without being told') is the natural form — the speaker doesn't need to be TOLD. This captures Onodera's dismissive tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 言わなくても means 'without saying', putting the subject on the speaker. 言わないでも is a non-standard variant.

contrast_examples.jp: 言われなくても知ってる。
何も言わないで帰った。
